references.text: Describes the various types of grain offerings baked in an oven, cooked on a griddle, or prepared in a pan—the same preparation methods mentioned in Lev 7:9.
Contains regulations concerning the grain offering and clarifies that it belongs to the priests, which is further elaborated in Lev 7:9.
Continues directly from verse 9 and describes the distribution of the dry grain offerings among Aaron's sons.
Confirms that the most holy offerings, including the grain offering, belong to the priests as their portion.
Ezekiel repeats the principle that the grain offering and other sacrifices belong to the priests.
Paul refers to the Old Testament principle that those who serve at the altar share in the sacrificial offerings.
